findings.title: Update prune.sh to consume the v2 manifest
findings.comment: Every successful snapshot now emits four fields, but prune.sh still reads three with `read -r epoch bytes path`. Its `path` therefore contains the byte count, a tab, and the archive path; the file check fails and rotation is silently skipped. An end-to-end run with BACKUP_KEEP=1 retained all four archives and reported success. Update the consumer to read all four columns and use the supplied label rather than recovering it from the filename.

findings.title: Shell-escape the remote directory and archive filename
findings.comment: BACKUP_REMOTE_DIR and the label-derived filename are interpolated into shell source sent to SSH. Surrounding them with single quotes does not escape embedded apostrophes: a directory containing `'; touch /tmp/marker; #` executes the injected command remotely, and an ordinary apostrophe in a directory or label also breaks replication. Escape both values for the remote shell or transfer them through a mechanism that does not interpolate them into executable shell source.

findings.title: Publish remote archives only after a complete transfer
findings.comment: The remote redirection opens the archive's final name before receiving any data. If SSH disconnects partway through, that name remains with a truncated payload even though the local run fails; a simulated interrupted transfer left a 16-byte .tar.gz under the final name. This contradicts the stated replication guarantee and makes incomplete files indistinguishable from completed replicas by name. Write to a remote staging file and rename it to the final name only after the transfer succeeds.

findings.title: Treat a zero force value as disabled
findings.comment: snapshot.sh initializes FORCE to `0` when BACKUP_FORCE is absent, but this condition tests whether the string is nonempty, so both `0` and `1` enable the override. Consequently, every ordinary run continues when either filesystem has insufficient space; a mocked df reporting zero available space reproduced successful archive creation without --force. Compare the value explicitly with `1`, or use an empty default consistently, so the documented fatal check operates unless requested otherwise.

findings.title: Restore exit and signal cleanup for the staging directory
findings.comment: The previous cleanup trap has been removed, and the staging directory is now deleted only after replication and publication succeed. A tar, SSH, or mv failure—or termination during those operations—leaves the partial or complete archive under TMPDIR. A failed replication reproduced a leftover directory containing the entire staged archive; recurring failures can accumulate full backups and exhaust the staging filesystem. Install cleanup immediately after make_stage succeeds and retain it for error and signal exits.

findings.title: Apply restrictive permissions on the replica host
findings.comment: The local `umask 077` is not propagated through SSH, so the remote mkdir and redirection use the remote account's default umask. With the common default of 022 and a newly created replica directory, archives are created as 0644 in a 0755 directory, exposing their contents to other users on the replica host despite local archives being private. Set a restrictive umask in the remote command and ensure the destination file remains private when replacing an existing archive.

explanation: incorrect — End-to-end checks reproduced disabled retention and low-space checks continuing without an override. Simulated SSH transfers also reproduced command injection, truncated published replicas, permissive remote file modes, and staging files left behind after failure; no live remote service was used.
